question: What powers the air compressor in an air brake system?
choice_a: A separate electric motor
choice_b: It is connected to the engine through gears or a v-belt
choice_c: The vehicle's hydraulic system
choice_d: A dedicated battery pack
explanation: The manual states the air compressor is connected to the engine through gears or a v-belt, and may be air cooled or cooled by the engine cooling system.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Air Compressor

question: At approximately what pressure does the governor cause the air compressor to stop pumping air ('cut-out')?
choice_a: Around 60 psi
choice_b: Around 45 psi
choice_c: Around 125 psi
choice_d: Around 250 psi
explanation: The manual states that when air tank pressure rises to the 'cut-out' level, around 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor from pumping air.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Air Compressor Governor

question: At approximately what pressure does the governor allow the compressor to start pumping again ('cut-in')?
choice_a: Around 20 psi
choice_b: Around 100 psi
choice_c: Around 60 psi
choice_d: Around 150 psi
explanation: The manual states that when tank pressure falls to the 'cut-in' pressure, around 100 psi, the governor allows the compressor to start pumping again.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Air Compressor Governor

question: Why do air brake systems include air storage tanks?
choice_a: To cool the compressed air before it reaches the brakes
choice_b: To filter fuel before it reaches the engine
choice_c: To store hydraulic brake fluid
choice_d: To hold compressed air so brakes can be used several times even if the compressor stops working
explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air and will hold enough to allow the brakes to be used several times, even if the compressor stops working.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Air Storage Tanks

question: Why is it important to drain air tanks?
choice_a: To recharge the alcohol evaporator
choice_b: Water and compressor oil collect in the tank and can freeze in cold weather, causing brake failure
choice_c: Draining is purely cosmetic maintenance
choice_d: To increase compressor cut-out pressure
explanation: Compressed air usually has water and compressor oil in it; the water can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure, so tanks must be drained completely.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Air Tank Drains

question: If your vehicle has manually operated air tank drain valves, when must you drain the tanks?
choice_a: Yourself, at the end of each day of driving
choice_b: Manual drains never need draining
choice_c: Only once a month
choice_d: Only before trips over 500 miles
explanation: Manually operated drain valves must be drained by the driver at the end of each day of driving.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Air Tank Drains

question: What is the purpose of an alcohol evaporator in an air brake system?
choice_a: To lubricate the air compressor
choice_b: To clean oil residue out of the brake chambers
choice_c: To put alcohol into the air system to reduce the risk of ice in air brake valves during cold weather
choice_d: To increase brake pad friction
explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator to put alcohol into the air system, reducing the risk of ice in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Alcohol Evaporator

question: A safety relief valve installed in the first tank the air compressor pumps to is usually set to open at what pressure?
choice_a: 200 psi
choice_b: 60 psi
choice_c: 150 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: The safety valve protects the tank and system from too much pressure and is usually set to open at 150 psi.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Safety Valve

question: What are two other names for the air brake pedal mentioned in the manual?
choice_a: Governor valve or relay valve
choice_b: Master cylinder or slave valve
choice_c: Foot valve or treadle valve
choice_d: Wig wag or tractor protection valve
explanation: The manual states the brake pedal is also called the foot valve or treadle valve.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, The Brake Pedal

question: What can happen if you press and release the brake pedal unnecessarily?
choice_a: It has no effect on air pressure
choice_b: It permanently damages the treadle valve
choice_c: Air can be let out of the system faster than the compressor can replace it, and if pressure gets too low the brakes won't work
choice_d: It automatically triggers the ABS malfunction lamp
explanation: Pressing and releasing the pedal unnecessarily can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it, and if pressure gets too low, the brakes won't work.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, The Brake Pedal

question: In an s-cam brake, what happens when air pressure moves the slack adjuster?
choice_a: It directly pushes a wedge between the brake shoes
choice_b: It twists the brake camshaft, turning the s-cam, which forces the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum
choice_c: It clamps a disc between brake lining pads like a c-clamp
choice_d: It releases alcohol into the brake lines
explanation: Air pressure moves the slack adjuster, twisting the brake camshaft and turning the s-cam, which forces the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Foundation Brakes (S-cam)

question: How do wedge brakes apply braking force?
choice_a: They use hydraulic fluid pressure instead of air
choice_b: The brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart against the brake drum
choice_c: They rely solely on a power screw and caliper
choice_d: They use an s-cam to rotate the brake shoes
explanation: In wedge brakes, the brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart and against the brake drum.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Foundation Brakes (Wedge Brakes)

question: In air-operated disc brakes, what does the brake chamber's pressure on the slack adjuster turn to clamp the disc?
choice_a: A power screw
choice_b: A wedge
choice_c: A treadle valve
choice_d: An s-cam
explanation: In air-operated disc brakes, the pressure of the brake chamber on the slack adjuster turns a power screw, which clamps the disc between the brake lining pads of a caliper.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Foundation Brakes (Disc Brakes)

question: On a vehicle with a dual air brake system, how are pressure gauges typically arranged?
choice_a: There is a gauge for each half of the system, or a single gauge with two needles
choice_b: Three gauges, one for each axle
choice_c: Dual systems have no supply pressure gauges
choice_d: Only one gauge total, with no distinction between systems
explanation: If the vehicle has a dual air brake system, there will be a gauge for each half of the system, or a single gauge with two needles.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Supply Pressure Gauges

question: What does it mean if you need increasing application pressure to hold the same speed?
choice_a: The brakes are fading, and you should slow down and use a lower gear
choice_b: The parking brake is still applied
choice_c: The ABS system has engaged normally
choice_d: The air compressor governor needs recalibration
explanation: Increasing application pressure to hold the same speed means the brakes are fading; you should slow down and use a lower gear.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Application Pressure Gauge

question: A visible low air pressure warning signal must come on before air pressure in the tanks falls below what level, on most vehicles?
choice_a: 100 psi
choice_b: 20 psi
choice_c: 60 psi
choice_d: 125 psi
explanation: A low air pressure warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Low Air Pressure Warning

question: On large buses, it is common for low pressure warning devices to signal at what pressure range?
explanation: The manual notes that on large buses it is common for the low pressure warning devices to signal at 80-85 psi.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Low Air Pressure Warning

question: What is a 'wig wag' warning device?
choice_a: A mechanical arm that drops into view when system pressure drops below 60 psi
choice_b: An audible-only alarm with no visual component
choice_c: A dashboard light that only activates the parking brake
choice_d: A device found only on ABS-equipped trailers
explanation: A wig wag device drops a mechanical arm into your view when the pressure in the system drops below 60 psi and rises out of view when pressure goes back above 60 psi.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Low Air Pressure Warning

question: How does the air brake system turn on the brake lights when the driver applies the brakes?
choice_a: With an electric switch that works by air pressure
choice_b: Brake lights on air brake vehicles must be activated manually
choice_c: Through the ABS malfunction lamp circuit
choice_d: Through a mechanical cable linked to the pedal
explanation: The stop light switch is an electric switch that works by air pressure and turns on the brake lights when the driver applies the air brakes.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Stop Light Switch

question: What is true about front brake limiting valves found on some vehicles made before 1975?
choice_a: They actually reduce the vehicle's stopping power, and the control should be kept in the 'normal' position
choice_b: They control the parking brake only
choice_c: They increase stopping power on ice
choice_d: They are required equipment on all modern vehicles
explanation: The manual states front brake limiting valves actually reduce the stopping power of the vehicle, since front wheel braking is good under all conditions, and the control should be kept in the 'normal' position.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Why must trucks, truck tractors, and buses be equipped with spring brakes for emergency and parking brake functions?
choice_a: Because spring brakes provide better fuel economy
choice_b: Because spring brakes replace the service brake entirely
choice_c: Because spring brakes are required only on vehicles built before 1975
choice_d: Because they must be held on by mechanical force, since air pressure can eventually leak away
explanation: Emergency and parking brakes must be held on by mechanical force because air pressure can eventually leak away; spring brakes are usually used to meet this need.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Spring Brakes

question: At what pressure range will tractor and straight truck spring brakes typically come fully on?
choice_a: 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi)
choice_b: 60 to 80 psi
choice_c: 100 to 125 psi
choice_d: 0 to 10 psi
explanation: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi, typically 20 to 30 psi.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Spring Brakes

question: Why should you never push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on?
choice_a: It has no effect either way
choice_b: It will trigger the ABS malfunction lamp
choice_c: The brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure
choice_d: It automatically releases the parking brake
explanation: The manual warns that pushing the brake pedal down when spring brakes are on could damage the brakes from the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Spring Brakes

question: On newer vehicles with air brakes, what shape and color is the parking brake control knob?
choice_a: A round, blue knob
choice_b: A square, red button
choice_c: A green toggle switch
choice_d: A diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull knob
explanation: In newer vehicles, you put on the parking brakes using a diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob; older vehicles may use a round blue knob or lever instead.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Parking Brake Controls

question: What does a modulating control valve allow a driver to do?
choice_a: Apply the spring brakes gradually, with more lever movement applying the brakes harder
choice_b: Instantly lock all wheels in an emergency
choice_c: Adjust the compressor cut-in pressure
choice_d: Bypass the low air pressure warning
explanation: A modulating control valve is spring-loaded and lets a driver apply the spring brakes gradually; the more the control lever is moved, the harder the spring brakes come on.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Spring Brakes (Modulating Control Valves)

question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date are required to be equipped with ABS?
choice_a: July 1, 2017
choice_b: January 1, 1994
choice_c: March 1, 1998
choice_d: March 1, 1997
explanation: The manual states truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Other air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) are required to have ABS if built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1994
choice_c: There is no such requirement
choice_d: March 1, 1997
explanation: Other air brake vehicles - trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies - built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps required to be?
choice_a: Blue
choice_b: Red
choice_c: Green
choice_d: Yellow
explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps to tell the driver if something isn't working.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Does ABS increase or decrease a vehicle's normal braking capability?
choice_a: Neither; ABS is an addition to normal brakes and only activates when wheels are about to lock up
choice_b: It always increases braking capability
choice_c: It replaces the normal braking system entirely
choice_d: It always decreases braking capability
explanation: ABS is an addition to your normal brakes; it does not decrease or increase your normal braking capability and only activates when wheels are about to lock up.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: In a dual air brake system, what do the two separate systems share?
choice_a: Nothing; they are entirely independent, including separate pedals
choice_b: A single set of brake controls
choice_c: A single brake pedal that only operates one system at a time, manually selected by the driver
choice_d: A single air tank
explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems, each with its own air tanks, hoses, and lines, which use a single set of brake controls.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Dual Air Brake Systems

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, you should allow time for the air compressor to build up at least what minimum pressure in both the primary and secondary systems?
choice_a: 60 psi
choice_b: 150 psi
choice_c: 100 psi
choice_d: 20 psi
explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Dual Air Brake Systems

question: During the walk-around inspection, how do you check slack adjusters on s-cam brakes?
choice_a: Check only the dashboard air pressure gauges
choice_b: Park on level ground, chock the wheels, release the parking brakes, and pull hard on each slack adjuster you can reach
choice_c: Rev the engine and listen for unusual noise
choice_d: Slack adjusters cannot be inspected without special tools
explanation: To check slack adjusters, park on level ground and chock the wheels, release the parking brakes so the slack adjusters can move, use gloves, and pull hard on each slack adjuster you can reach.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Inspecting Air Brake Systems

question: If a slack adjuster moves more than about how far where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment?
choice_a: About one-quarter inch
choice_b: About one inch
choice_c: About six inches
choice_d: Any movement at all means failure
explanation: If a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Inspecting Air Brake Systems

question: Since what year have all vehicles been built with automatic slack adjusters, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states all vehicles built since 1994 have automatic slack adjusters, though they must still be checked.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Inspecting Air Brake Systems

question: Why is manual adjustment of an automatic slack adjuster considered dangerous except as a temporary emergency measure?
choice_a: It has no real risk associated with it
choice_b: It voids the vehicle's warranty automatically
choice_c: It may give the driver a false sense of security about the brake system's effectiveness without fixing the underlying problem
choice_d: It is illegal in all circumstances
explanation: Manual adjustment of an automatic adjuster is dangerous because it may give the driver a false sense of security regarding the effectiveness of the braking system without fixing the underlying adjustment problem.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Inspecting Air Brake Systems

question: What is the limit on crack length for brake drums or discs during inspection?
choice_a: Cracks must not be longer than one half the width of the friction area
choice_b: Crack length is not addressed in inspections
choice_c: No cracks of any length are permitted, however small
choice_d: Cracks up to the full width of the friction area are acceptable
explanation: Brake drums or discs must not have cracks longer than one half the width of the friction area.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Inspecting Air Brake Systems

question: During the final air brake check, at approximately what pressure should the air compressor governor cut-out the compressor?
choice_a: About 45 psi
choice_b: About 60 psi
choice_c: About 125 psi
choice_d: About 20 psi
explanation: During the final check, pumping by the compressor should start at about 100 psi, and the governor should cut-out the compressor at about 125 psi (per manufacturer specification).
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Final Air Brake Check

question: What is the maximum allowable air leakage rate for a single (non-combination) vehicle with a fully-charged system, engine off, and parking brake released?
choice_a: Less than two psi in one minute
choice_b: Any leakage is disqualifying
choice_c: Less than three psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than ten psi in one minute
explanation: The manual states the loss rate should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles when testing air leakage rate.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Final Air Brake Check

question: What is the maximum allowable air leakage rate for a combination vehicle under the same test conditions?
choice_a: Less than two psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than ten psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than one psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than three psi in one minute
explanation: The loss rate should be less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles when testing the air leakage rate.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Final Air Brake Check

question: When fully applying the foot brake and holding it for one minute with the engine off, how much pressure drop is acceptable for a single vehicle before you must check for leaks?
choice_a: No more than three pounds in one minute
choice_b: No more than four pounds in one minute
choice_c: No more than ten pounds in one minute
choice_d: No pressure drop is ever acceptable
explanation: With the foot brake fully applied for one minute, the air pressure should not drop more than three psi in one minute for a single vehicle (four psi for a combination vehicle).
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Final Air Brake Check

question: In a dual air system, how quickly should air pressure build from 85 to 100 psi at operating rpm?
choice_a: Within 3 minutes
choice_b: Within 45 seconds
choice_c: Within 10 seconds
choice_d: Within 5 minutes
explanation: In dual air systems, at operating rpm the pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Final Air Brake Check

question: How do you test the parking brake during an air brake inspection?
choice_a: Check only that the warning light is off
choice_b: Stop the vehicle, apply the parking brake, and gently pull against it in a low gear to confirm it holds
choice_c: Drive at highway speed and slam on the parking brake
choice_d: The parking brake cannot be tested without a mechanic
explanation: To test the parking brake, stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that it will hold.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Final Air Brake Check

question: What is the 'controlled braking' method for an emergency stop?
choice_a: Release the brakes completely and steer around the hazard
choice_b: Pump the brakes rapidly and continuously
choice_c: Apply the brakes fully, release when wheels lock, then reapply fully once wheels roll again
choice_d: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, keeping steering movements small
explanation: With controlled braking, you apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small while doing this.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Emergency Stops

question: What is the 'stab braking' method?
choice_a: Apply light, steady pressure throughout the stop
choice_b: Apply the brakes all the way, release when wheels lock up, then reapply fully once wheels start rolling again
choice_c: Alternate between the accelerator and brake pedal rapidly
choice_d: Only use the parking brake in an emergency
explanation: With stab braking, you apply the brakes all the way, release when the wheels lock up, and apply the brakes fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Emergency Stops

question: What four factors make up total stopping distance for a vehicle with air brakes?
choice_a: Perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance
choice_b: Brake lag distance and braking distance only
choice_c: Perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance only (no brake lag)
choice_d: Reaction distance and braking distance only
explanation: Total stopping distance equals perception distance plus reaction distance plus brake lag distance plus braking distance.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Stopping Distance

question: About how much distance does air brake lag add at 55 mph on dry pavement?
choice_a: About 32 feet
choice_b: About 100 feet
choice_c: About 450 feet
choice_d: About 5 feet
explanation: The air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet, contributing to a total stopping distance over 450 feet.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Stopping Distance

question: What causes brake fade according to the manual?
choice_a: Cold weather causing the brake fluid to thicken
choice_b: Excessive use of the service brakes causing overheating, which leads to chemical changes in the brake lining and drum expansion
choice_c: Underinflated tires
choice_d: Using the parking brake too often
explanation: Excessive use of the service brakes results in overheating and leads to brake fade, caused by chemical changes in the brake lining and expansion of the overheated brake drums.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Brake Fading or Failure

question: On a long or steep downgrade, after applying the brakes hard enough to feel a definite slowdown, when should you release them?
choice_a: When your speed drops 20 mph below your safe speed
choice_b: When your speed drops to about five mph below your 'safe' speed, holding the application for about three seconds
choice_c: You should never release the brakes until reaching the bottom of the grade
choice_d: Exactly one mph below your safe speed
explanation: The proper technique is to apply the brakes hard enough to feel a definite slowdown, then release when speed is reduced to about five mph below your 'safe' speed, with the application lasting about three seconds.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Proper Braking Technique

question: Why should you avoid using the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot or very wet in freezing temperatures?
choice_a: It is only a suggestion with no real consequence
choice_b: Hot brakes can be damaged by the heat, and wet brakes in freezing temperatures can freeze so the vehicle cannot move
choice_c: It voids the manufacturer's warranty
choice_d: Parking brakes automatically disengage when hot
explanation: If brakes are used while very hot, they can be damaged by the heat; if used in freezing temperatures when very wet, they can freeze so the vehicle cannot move.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Parking Brakes

question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning signal comes on while driving?
choice_a: Ignore it unless the buzzer also sounds
choice_b: Stop and safely park the vehicle as soon as possible
choice_c: Increase speed to reach a repair facility faster
choice_d: Continue driving normally since spring brakes will eventually engage
explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, you should stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible, since there might be an air leak in the system.
source_note: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Louisiana DPS/OMV -- Section 5, Air Brakes, Low Air Pressure
